title: Barista Pro stops after a few seconds and beeps: your next step

questions.text: With no portafilter fitted, run hot water, then press 1 CUP into a cup. What happens?
options: Both run normally (hot water runs about 60 seconds)
Hot water or 1 CUP stops after a few seconds with beeps
The machine is on but won't do anything

questions.text: Is the water tank pushed down until it locks, and filled above MIN?
options: Yes, and it still cuts out

questions.text: Have you repeated the hot-water test with the water filter taken out?
options: Yes, and then it ran normally
Yes, and it still cut out
I don't use a water filter

questions.text: Have you run the on-screen DESCALE cycle since this started?
options: Yes, and it still cuts out

questions.text: Have you tried RESET DEFAULTS from the menu?
options: Yes, and it still cuts out

questions.text: Where is your machine on cover?
options: Brand new, still inside the return window

dial-in.title: Keep your machine: it's the puck, not the machine
dial-in.text: Water flows normally, so the water path is fine. The booklet's causes for a shot that won't flow are a grind that's too fine, too much coffee, tamping too hard or a blocked basket. Grind a few steps coarser, check the dose, and clear the basket holes with the cleaning-tool pin.

cool-down.title: Let it cool: this looks like the thermal cut-out
cool-down.text: Switch it off, unplug it and let it cool for 30 to 60 minutes. That's the booklet's fix for a machine that is on but has stopped working. If it still won't run after that, contact the manufacturer's support.

tank.title: Seat the tank and fill it above MIN
tank.text: Push the tank down until it locks, then fill it above MIN. The booklet says an empty or unseated tank stops the water and can make the pump run loudly with nothing coming out. Then run the hot-water test again.

filter-test.title: Run the hot-water test without the water filter
filter-test.text: Take the filter out of the tank and run hot water again with no portafilter fitted. If it now runs the full 60 seconds, the filter was the problem. Soak a new filter in cold water for 5 minutes before you fit it.

new-filter.title: Keep your machine: replace the water filter
new-filter.text: The filter was the problem. Soak a new one in cold water for 5 minutes before fitting it. One edition of the booklet says to replace it every 2 months and the other every 3, and more often if your water is hard. A new filter is the only thing you need to buy.

descale.title: Run the DESCALE cycle
descale.text: Take the filter out and run the on-screen DESCALE cycle, then its rinse. The booklet gives scale as a cause of no water flow and no steam. If the machine runs normally afterwards, keep it and descale whenever the alert shows.

reset.title: Try RESET DEFAULTS, then test again
reset.text: Press MENU, choose RESET DEFAULTS, then run the hot-water test again. It's free and harmless, but it only resets your grind, dose, temperature and shot-volume settings, so don't expect much from it.

return.title: Return or exchange it
return.text: On a brand-new machine still inside its return window, take it back rather than keep troubleshooting. The booklet doesn't cover this fault. Owners and one repairer link it to the flow meter or its wiring, and that isn't something to fix at home.

claim.title: Stop here and contact the manufacturer's support
claim.text: Don't open the machine: repairs by unauthorised parties can cost you the claim. Contact the manufacturer's support through their support page, not the store. Have the batch code from the sticker under or on the back of the machine and your receipt ready. If you're not sure you're covered, they can tell you.

repair-or-replace.title: Get a written quote, then decide on repair or replace
repair-or-replace.text: Owners and one repairer point to the flow meter or its wiring. Don't open it yourself. Get a written quote and ask for a genuine part, because the repairer warns against generic copies. Compare the quote with the cost of a new machine. One owner's repair failed again about seven months later, so a high quote favours replacing.
